column3: Which selectable part of the package puts this file there, the
Windows package's features under the names the two POSIX routes
use for them. service is everything the package is for and is not
selectable. The optional providers of VISION 2026-09-22 are:
localstores, inventoryd and the declaration that declares it,
installed unless the person says otherwise because it only reads;
modelhost, modelhostd alone, installed only when asked for — the
declaration is written later by openabstractions models host, so
this package ships none; mcpgateway, the stdio MCP server,
installed only when asked for.
On Linux install.sh reads the FEATURES file this column generates
and installs the chosen ones. On macOS each optional feature is
its own component package and its own choice in the installer
where it lands, relative to the person's home directory. On macOS
that is the payload tree pkgbuild is handed; on Linux it is the
tree install.sh copies out of the tarball.
gobuild    go build the package at <from> in <source>, unless --bin
names a directory that already holds the built programs
swiftbuild swiftc the single file at <from> in <source>, macOS only,
unless --bin names a directory that already holds it
copy       take the file at <from> out of <source>
authored   written here, in installer/posix/, and shipped as it stands
generated  written by build.py; <from> is "-"
license    the file --license names; <source> is posix and <from> is "-".
The one LICENSE at a repository root is the whole obligation,
and which root that is depends on which repository is being
built, so it is an argument rather than a source id

column1: > The Panel is here for macOS, four rows below: the app bundle's own files, in
> the service feature like the Windows package's Tools bundling, because it is
> not a person's choice, only whether it built. It is not here for Linux, which
> ships no GUI (research/panel-native/DECISION.md). The C++ header is not here
> either — bindings/download-over-curl publishes from nowhere. The Windows
> package gates it away and says so; that one row carries no path here, and the
> @BIN@ in an authored file is the absolute directory openabstractions lands in.
> install.sh on Linux and scripts/postinstall on macOS substitute it. Nothing
> else is substituted at install time anywhere.
> A source with no --src has its rows left out of the package and each one named,
> the way the Windows build gates the UNRESOLVED rows. A runtime program is never
> left out that way: a runtime gobuild row with neither --src nor --bin stops the
> build. That is what lets a package built only from published module versions
> ship openabstractions without checking out any repository. An optional
> feature's program is different: a build that cannot obtain it leaves that whole
> feature out, names it, and the package that results offers one fewer choice
> rather than failing. jobd, dl, jobctl, the jobd sweep units and the Python
> file-store packages leave the payload in 0.2.0 (docs/REMOVED.md).
